# OBS008 `deprecated-character-syntax`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

Old-style character length `character*n` / `character*(*)`.

## Why

The `character*n` form is obsolescent since Fortran 95. `character(len=n)` is the modern form and
is consistent with every other kind and length parameter.

## Reported

```fortran
character*20 :: name
```

## Preferred

```fortran
character(len=20) :: name
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS008] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS008` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB061` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
